cases.title: Can Nathaniel's Rockland family rejoin the main Beverage tree?
cases.place: North Fox Island / North Haven / Rockland, Maine
cases.status: OPEN — probable research lead; original parentage not proved
cases.question: Did the Nathaniel who married Sarah Alexander in 1838 have parents John White Beverage and Rachel Lucy Crosby, and was he the nephew of Capt. Matthew as the 1865 history states?
cases.working_theory: A collaborative compilation supplies the precise John White/Rachel parent pair; existing tree indexes those parents but currently records no Nathaniel child. Eaton separately says Nathaniel is a nephew of Capt. Matthew.
cases.strong_evidence: 1865 Eaton's published nephew/niece description is an explicit historical claim; 1803 parentage is derivative only.
cases.not_proved: No original 1803 North Haven/Vinalhaven birth register, 1838 marriage return, parent-named probate or direct ancestral bridge inspected; do not add father or mother or connect graph components.
next_checks: Find the actual 20 October 1803 town birth/baptism entry and transcribe both parents, volume/page and original witness.
Check 26 April 1838 Nathaniel–Sarah Alexander original marriage return for parties, occupations, residence and witnesses.
Compare 1865 Eaton's nephew and niece language with Thomas/Matthew sibling evidence; test affine vs blood relationship.
Check John White Beverage's 1839 estate/probate for son Nathaniel, not merely a same-surname witness.
cases.research_value: Highest-priority possible bridge: an original named-parent entry could reconnect an established Rockland group without speculation.

cases.title: Did the 1785 Fox Islands minor Matthew become the later Hope captain?
cases.status: OPEN — no original manuscript parentage; DO NOT connect
cases.question: Who was the 'Matthew Beveridge a minor' in the 1785 settlers petition, and is there an original document naming his parents?
cases.working_theory: Published later histories place a minor Matthew among James and Thomas in 1785, while another retrospective book calls Matthew a younger brother of Thomas.
cases.strong_evidence: 1889 petition transcription documents a named minor; the separately cataloged 1786 Putnam manuscript might preserve settlement years and parcel details.
cases.not_proved: Co-occurrence on a petition is not sibling proof, no source establishes birth parents, and the unreviewed 1820 census does not equate the minor with the 1837 decedent.
next_checks: Retrieve Massachusetts Archives SC1/Series 228 original 1785 petition and signatures/annotations, not just the 1889 printing.
Read Rufus Putnam's 18 March 1786 manuscript report/settlers' lot list from Maine State Archives Box 001.
Compare exact settlement parcels, ages and residence sequence with identified Hope records and pre-1785 Topsham originals.
Do not add a parent, sibling or generational connection until an original contemporary identity bridge is documented.
cases.research_value: Potential eighteenth-century origin connection but higher uncertainty; preserve as an open historical identity question.
